status: OPEN - extraction code may not be written
rule: Anything still UNVERIFIED when this gate closes is named as unverified in the fixture manifest. Writing it down a second time does not promote it.

blocker.statement: fact-to-rendered-evidence binding still requires empirical validation
blocker.note: This replaces an earlier and wronger statement of the blocker as 'SEC primary sources are unavailable'. Unreachability from one environment is not a property of the source, and describing it as one turned a local network condition into a permanent-sounding fact. The access questions are settled; what is unsettled is whether a structured fact can be bound to a location in the rendered filing, and at what coverage.

verified.authentication: none - no API key is required
verified.reuse: public EDGAR filing content may be reused
verified.inline_xbrl: Inline XBRL embeds machine-readable facts directly inside the human-readable filing document

sec.still_to_measure: Whether those embedded facts can be matched to a visible location reliably enough to serve as gold evidence, and at what coverage. That is empirical and is not answered by any documentation.

working_hypothesis.truth: a fact from CompanyFacts / the structured API
working_hypothesis.explicit_non_assumption: The official API is NOT assumed to return a rendered page or a span location. The binding is something to be measured on real filings, not read off an endpoint.

measurement_plan.note: Run on real filing samples before any extractor is written. Each step yields a rate with a denominator, not a yes or no.
steps: taxonomy concept / context / unit / value / period matching
measurement_plan.fallback: If anchor coverage is insufficient, fall back to located spans: only an exact, unambiguous single match becomes gold; ambiguous and unmatched facts are excluded and counted; the exclusion rate is published.
measurement_plan.forbidden: Storing an inferred gold evidence location. A guessed anchor is worse than an excluded one, because an exclusion is visible in the denominator and a guess is indistinguishable from evidence.

verified.returns: single company, FULL financial statements - the multi-account endpoint the contract asked whether existed
verified.why_it_matters: account_id is the taxonomy element identifier, so a fact arrives already keyed to a concept. That is half of what a gold label needs; the other half is where in the document it is stated.

verified.returns: multiple companies, key accounts only - despite the name, not full accounts for one company
the raw XBRL for one filing, as a ZIP
taxonomy metadata - account id, Korean and English labels, data type, IFRS paragraph references. No company figures.
the original filing as a ZIP, not structured JSON

request_limit.canonical_wording: General documented threshold is approximately 20,000 requests; the effective limit may vary by account/configuration.
request_limit.do_not_record: A fixed 10,000/day or 20,000/day. The official terms page states that a limit exists without naming it, and the FAQ answer renders in a JavaScript modal that could not be fetched. Treating either circulating figure as exact would put a number in the fixture's request budget that nobody has read from the source.

opendart.terms: FSS holds copyright in the API; the filing belongs to its submitter; FSS does not warrant accuracy; statistical, promotional and academic research use is a permitted exception. No explicit redistribution prohibition was found.

crux_fact_to_document_location.question: Can a structured fact be bound to its evidence location in the rendered filing, and at what coverage?

united_states.mechanism: Inline XBRL embeds machine-readable facts inside the human-readable document, so the binding is expected to be recoverable by parsing the iXBRL DOM.
united_states.status: UNMEASURED - this is the blocker, and it is empirical
united_states.note: Do not assume an official endpoint supplies the location. The mechanism existing and the binding being reliable at usable coverage are different claims.

korea.basis: None of fnlttSinglAcntAll, fnlttMultiAcnt, fnlttXbrl or xbrlTaxonomy documents any field linking an XBRL element to a position in the filed document: no HTML element id, no rendering link, no page or coordinate.
korea.remaining_cheap_check: Download the document.xml ZIP for one real filing and inspect its internal HTML/XBRL for element ids. Needs an OpenDART key and nothing else. This is the last inexpensive place a Korean anchor could be hiding.

next_action.unblocked: Run the six measurement steps above on real SEC filing samples. No API key is needed; a declared User-Agent is, and automated access stays at or under 10 requests per second.
next_action.cheap_and_pending: Inspect one OpenDART document.xml ZIP once a key exists.
next_action.not_permitted_yet: Any extraction code. INTAKE-0103 is OPEN until the binding is measured.
